start.topic: Perimeter of rectangles, squares and polygons
start.opening: Namaste Kabir, main Asha, aapki AI teacher. Aaj perimeter seekhenge. Aap maths mein kaunsa topic kar rahe hain?

turns.line: rectangle ke chaaron sides jodenge, 50 plus 30 plus 50 plus 30, 160 metre
turns.reply: Kabir, aapne chaaron sides jodkar sahi method lagaya: 50 plus 30 plus 50 plus 30, total 160 metre. Ab bataiye, square mein kya jodenge?
Kabir, yahan step toota: rectangle ka perimeter 2 guna length plus breadth nahi; length aur breadth ka yog 2 se multiply hota hai. Formula bataiye.
Theek hai, Kabir. Rectangle ka perimeter: 2 guna, length plus breadth. Ab 50 metre aur 30 metre se formula lagaiye.

record.summary:
Kabir practised finding a rectangle’s perimeter by adding all four sides.
Kabir calculated 50 + 30 + 50 + 30 as 160 metres.
Kabir also stated the formula as 2 × length + breadth.
Kabir said they understood and were ready to continue.
record.parentNote: Kabir practised finding a rectangle’s perimeter by adding the four sides and obtained 160 metres for the given measurements. Kabir also recalled a shortcut formula, but the wording was incomplete: it should be 2 × (length + breadth). At home, Kabir can practise writing the full formula with brackets and checking it against addition of all four sides.
